explanation: Take the first preorder value as the root, find it by scanning inorder, and slice both traversals into the corresponding left and right portions. Recursively construct those subtrees and attach them to a new root.
timeComplexity: O(n squared) worst-case time: a skew tree repeatedly searches and copies traversal slices of sizes n,n-1,...,1. Balanced trees take O(n log(n+1)) with this slicing implementation.
spaceComplexity: O(n squared) worst-case auxiliary space: ancestor frames retain traversal slices of sizes n,n-1,... along a skew recursion chain. The newly allocated n tree nodes are output space.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The first preorder entry is the current root. Its unique inorder position gives the exact number and values of left-subtree nodes, so the next that-many preorder entries belong to the left subtree and the remainder to the right. The slices preserve both traversal orders; induction reconstructs the unique valid tree.
walkthrough: For preorder [8,3,1,6,10,9] and inorder [1,3,6,8,9,10], root 8 splits inorder after three values. Slice preorder into [3,1,6] and [10,9]; those roots become 3 with children 1,6 and 10 with left child 9. Return level order [8,3,10,1,6,9].
edgeCases: Values are distinct and both traversals contain the same set.
Empty traversals reconstruct an empty tree.
A root at an inorder endpoint creates an empty child subtree.
